questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was very interested in the courses at the university’s. The location was also important to me, since I wanted to be close to nature. Then I also chose actually based on the universities webpage. I wanted to go somewhere where they were prepared for exchange students and the information was easy to find and understand.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was so happy with the university, the nature around it and the many danish people I met. I really prioritised getting to know danish people, so that I would have friends to share the experience with, when I got home. This is probably the thing that I’m most grateful for.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think it was very easy. We got a lot of emails from the school, and I feel like we where well informed and in time.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Many information emails and meet ups with all the exchange students. So many gatherings of different kinds, so that we could get to know each other.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Me and three other girls quickly decided that we wanted to live together. Shortly after we got accepted by Copenhagen University, we began looking, and made our booking already in November, over 6 months before we were going on exchange. I would recommend beginning to look for places as early as possible.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you don’t live close to campus, you will probably need to take the bus, which is also very good. But biking in the city is not really that recommended. Cars are not that used to bikes and also there is a lot of hills:))

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: After acceptance by Copenhagen University, we waited until May when the registration opened at the host University. Then we applied and shortly after received an email with the acceptance letter. It was very easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We where in contact with the help centre for international students, and they where very helpful and quick to reply.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was very successful. I got all the courses that I wanted. They give you a date and time for when the registration opens, and then we were quick to sign up for the courses we wanted. We didn’t even need to hurry that much, we all got the courses we wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Really look at the schedules for the courses before registering. In their system they have a function, where you can create your own schedules, and that was very helpful. Also, if you want as few hours a week as possible, don’t choose courses that has laboratory work. You can find all this information at Uvics website under courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took third and fourth year courses. None of them were that difficult, and I was really happy with the teaching method and the material.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
My courses were only based on learning from the lectures, and we had no reading homework. I was really fond of this method. Also, we had midterms and reports which was grated and counted in the final grade. This was an amazing experience. The final exam usually counted for between 30-40% of the final grade, which took a lot of pressure off us. 
Also, we learned everything way better, since we had to do a lot of work along the way, which also made me rember everything way better.
I would hope that Copenhagen University will do it like this one day.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
MICR410 - Microbiota and Human Health
ES361 - The Biodiversity of British Columbia 
BIOL388 - Applied Molecular Biology
AE303A - Introduction to Ceramics and wheel techniques

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Microbiota and human health were very well structured, and amazing teacher and very interesting topics. The midterms are two tat home quizzes with all aids allows, very easy. And the we had to do a research paper, which was very cool to try.

Ceramics was fun and it was nice to have something different. It is a lot of work though, so don’t expect it to be easy and quickly over with.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: It was really easy and cheap to rent cars for going on trips, so we ended up doing that a lot. I also feel in love with surfing, and that is a bit expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Grocery’s were more expensive. Takeout where less. Uber and car rentals was also cheaper than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: So many clubs, you could choose every sport and every hobby. They had everything from sailing, climbing, river rafting, surfing, baking, Taylor swift, book clubs, outdoor club.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join a club, any club! It was a cool way to get to know the locals and your fellow exchange students. Especially the outdoor club did some fun stuff, but it is very popular, so don’t hesitate to sign up!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go around the island! Go surfing and hiking in Torino. Visit telegraph cove and Strathcona National Park in the summer. Go to salts spring island. Go to whistler and Squamish. Go to Banff National park!!! Amazing experience. Just really get around and see stuff, that is so fun. Visit Vancouver one day. Go whalewhatching!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join clubs! Go to Lucky Mondays:))

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: They students are in general younger when they start Univeristy, so sometimes I felt a bit of an age barrier.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How respectful they were about the indigenous people and their heritage. They are very friendly and genuinely interested in what you are telling them. People are very sweet.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Research housing as early as possible.
Do courses that has the workload that you can manage when living abroad, it can be overwhelming.
Do a fun course that only exists at Uvic, that is so fun to try.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You will spend more money than you think, but don’t let it put limits on you! This is a once in a lifetime experience, so do it just they way you want to!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Exploring the nature of Canada and meeting my now really close danish friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Dealing with all your problems in a whole new setting with all new people. You will have tough days and it is really important to find someone you trust and can share with.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
